response.justification: Strong, versatile senior engineer with 15+ years of delivery experience, but the profile does not match the core requirements of this role. The position demands 8 years of C++ programming; the resume shows roughly six months of C/C++ work at National Instruments plus a university thesis project, with the rest of the career centered on TypeScript/Node.js, D, and web/full-stack development. Large-scale distributed systems exposure exists (Sociomantic/Dunnhumby, high-throughput low-latency services) but is limited to a ~2-year window and not in C++ or cloud compute platform architecture. There is also no evidence of a formal technical leadership role mentoring cloud/DevOps engineers or owning platform-level technical strategy, though founding GISCollective and running workshops shows leadership potential. A gap this large on the hard minimum qualification makes this a poor fit for a compute-platform technical lead.
strengths: Deep, broad engineering experience across backend, embedded, web and infrastructure
Proven high-throughput, low-latency systems work at Sociomantic/Dunnhumby
Strong mentoring and knowledge-sharing record via workshops, courses, and OSS projects
concerns: C++ experience far below the 8-year minimum (~6 months professional)
No formal technical leadership or platform-strategy ownership role
Limited cloud compute platform / large-scale infrastructure architecture depth

key_factors.factor: Lack of formal technical leadership role
